incidents.cause: The total loss of engine power due to an insufficient fastener preload that led to the failure of the No. 2 connecting rod assembly.

The pilot's failure to maintain the proper airspeed during a low altitude aerial application maneuver and his exceedance of the airplane’s critical angle of attack, which resulted in an aerodymanic stall at too low of an altiutde to recover.
The pilot’s failure to extend the landing gear before landing due to his distraction with the wind gusts.
The loss of engine power for reasons undetermined.
The pilot's inadequate landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing during crosswind conditions.
The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during the landing approach in gusty wind conditions.
The student pilot’s improper flight control inputs and the flight instructor’s delayed remedial action during takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion and impact with terrain.
The student pilot’s loss of directional control during the landing roll.
A landing gear brake malfunction during the landing for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
A separation of the left rudder cable due to inadequate maintenance, which resulted in an in-flight loss of control and impact with terrain.

The pilot's improper engine modification and operation, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation, and the pilot's failure to maintain an adequate approach path, which resulted in the airplane landing short of the runway.
